channel.title: Dr. Yasas Sri Wickramasinghe
channel.description: Augmented reality research, teaching and writing from Dr. Yasas Sri Wickramasinghe.

item.title: VRST 2026 — The Role of Display Type and Camera Perspective in Shaping VR Presence and Motion Sickness
item.description: I'm presenting my paper "The Role of Display Type and Camera Perspective in Shaping VR Presence and Motion Sickness" at the 32nd ACM Symposium on Virtual Reality Software and Technology (VRST 2026), held at the Research Institute of Electrical Communication, Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan, 16-18 November 2026. My presentation slot is still to be confirmed by the organisers.

item.title: The Madagaskar Effect: I Hid One Line My Students Couldn't See. Their AI Obeyed It.
item.description: A made-up term hidden in white text showed me who read their AI's answer and who didn't. The method, why students skip the read, and a toolkit for educators.

item.title: iPhone Duo Design Guidelines: What Netflix’s Foldable App Gets Right
item.description: Netflix rebuilt its app for Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo. What it changed, Apple’s new iPhone Duo design guidelines in plain English, and what it means for HCI.

item.title: PHP2Shell Explained: Is Your Website Wide Open?
item.description: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) in plain English: what the two PHP flaws are, why they matter, which versions are fixed, and what to do today.

item.title: If a Machine Can Make You Feel You Did Something You Didn’t, Who Decides the Timing?
item.description: Muscle stimulation fired 160 ms after a cue made people react 80 ms faster, and it still felt like their own move. What five HCI studies mean for design.

item.title: In a Blink: VR Researchers Turned the World and Nobody Noticed
item.description: Researchers rotated virtual worlds 2–5° during people's blinks and nobody noticed. How it works, Apple's blink patent, and why eye data needs care.

item.title: New Zealand Scholarships 2027: Deadlines Sri Lankans Can't Miss
item.description: Want to study in New Zealand in 2027? Here are the scholarships open now at UC, Auckland, Waikato, Victoria and AUT, with the real dates and amounts, and what to do first.

item.title: The Invisible Keyboard Hiding Under Your iPhone Keyboard
item.description: Your fingertip covers about three iPhone keys, yet you type the right letter. Inside Apple's hidden hit regions, touch research, and lessons for designers.

item.title: Slides: Designing Shared Worlds Across Distance (NZGDC 2026)
item.description: The slides from my NZGDC 2026 talk are online as a free PDF — all 30, covering the three multiplayer AR games, the numbers from 128 players and the six rules I'd now build any remote AR game around. The talk page also has the papers behind each study, an interactive view-cone demo and the Q&A.

item.title: NZGDC 2026 — Designing Shared Worlds Across Distance
item.description: I spoke at NZGDC 2026 in Auckland on "Designing Shared Worlds Across Distance: Lessons from Multiplayer AR Game Research" — what three multiplayer AR games and 128 players taught me about playing together from apart, and six rules for designing remote AR games. 1 October 2026, 3:00–3:30 PM, NZ International Convention Centre, Auckland. The slides, the six rules and the papers are on the talk page.

item.title: From Research to Reality — AR/VR Entrepreneurship Opportunities for Sri Lankans
item.description: I spoke at an IEEE Entrepreneurship, Sri Lanka Section session on how AR/VR research can become real-world entrepreneurial opportunities, covering the AR/VR startup landscape and the opportunities open to Sri Lankan innovators. 22 September 2026, 3:30 PM (Sri Lanka time), online via Zoom.

item.title: ICITR 2026 — Workshop 01: Designing Shared Worlds Across Distance
item.description: I'm leading Workshop 01 of ICITR 2026 — the 11th International Conference on Information Technology Research (1–2 December 2026), organised by the Information Technology Research Unit at the University of Moratuwa, Sri Lanka. "Designing Shared Worlds Across Distance: What Multiplayer AR Research Taught Me" explores the design and development of location-based multiplayer AR games, and how augmented reality becomes a core gameplay mechanic that connects remote players. Planned as an online session; scheduled for 27 November 2026, 1:00–4:00 PM (Sri Lanka time).

item.title: CODE with WIE 2026 — Workshop 01: Architecting the Augmented Tomorrow
item.description: Workshop 01 of CODE with WIE 2026, hosted by IEEE Women in Engineering Sri Lanka — exploring the technologies shaping the future and how innovation is transforming tomorrow's world, drawn from research in immersive technologies, software product engineering and game design. Online via Google Meet.

item.title: I Built a Free Website to Help Sri Lankan Drivers Save Thousands on Fuel
item.description: The story behind a free website built to help drivers in Sri Lanka find ways to save on fuel costs. Covers the motivation for the project and what it took to build and ship it.

item.title: Research Visit to Tohoku University — Building an NZ–Japan AR Collaboration
item.description: Prof. Rob Lindeman and I (HIT Lab NZ, University of Canterbury) visited the Interactive Content Design Lab at the Research Institute of Electrical Communication (RIEC), Tohoku University, Sendai, Japan. We presented our research on location-based augmented reality and immersive interaction, and explored a joint research project bridging New Zealand and Japan.

item.title: Selected for Falling Walls Lab Aotearoa New Zealand 2024
item.description: One of nineteen researchers and innovators chosen from across Aotearoa New Zealand and the Pacific to pitch a breakthrough idea in three minutes at Falling Walls Lab Aotearoa New Zealand 2024, organised by Royal Society Te Apārangi. Pitch: "Breaking the Wall of Loneliness through Play" — how location-based augmented reality games can bring people together and ease loneliness through shared experiences.

item.title: New Zealand Campervan Road Trip
item.description: A personal account of a campervan road trip through New Zealand. A change of pace from the technical writing — travel notes and reflections from the road.

item.title: Start a Money-Making Blog on Ghost
item.description: A practical walkthrough of starting a blog on the Ghost publishing platform with monetisation in mind. Covers the basics of setup and the choices that shape whether a blog can sustain itself.

item.title: Hand Tracking in Augmented Reality
item.description: An overview of how hand-tracking technology works in AR and why it matters for natural, controller-free interaction. Looks at the techniques and challenges behind tracking hand movement and gestures in real time.

item.title: Black Friday Gift Ideas for Him or Her in 2022
item.description: A lighter, seasonal piece with Black Friday gift ideas. A departure from the technical essays — practical, timely shopping suggestions.
